blocks.text: Explains that Part 3 added list_dir and read_file and Part 4 added write_file, delete, and execute_command. States the key invariant: by the time a mutating tool_call reaches this module the backend has already confirmed it. Documents the full tool_call / tool_result JSON protocol including every tool name and its params shape.
blocks.title: Module docstring: scope, the propose/confirm contract, and message shapes

blocks.text: Four constants cap the daemon's resource usage: MAX_READ_FILE_BYTES (1 MB per file read), MAX_WRITE_FILE_BYTES (1 MB per write), DEFAULT_EXECUTE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (30 s), MAX_EXECUTE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s), and MAX_EXECUTE_OUTPUT_CHARS (200 000 chars per stream). Each comment explains why the same "runaway X must not block the shared connection" reasoning applies.
blocks.title: Module-level caps

blocks.text: ToolError is a plain Exception whose message is always user-safe (never a raw traceback). _resolve calls assert_within_root and re-raises PathGuardError as ToolError. list_dir resolves the path, checks existence and directory-ness, then scans entries with sorted iterdir (dirs first, then files alphabetically by lowercase name); a single unreadable entry falls back to type='unknown' rather than failing the whole listing.
blocks.title: ToolError, _resolve, and list_dir

blocks.anchor: def read_file(root: Path, path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
blocks.text: read_file reads up to MAX_READ_FILE_BYTES, decodes as UTF-8 (raising ToolError for binary files), and returns path, content, size, and truncated. write_file encodes to UTF-8 first to enforce the byte cap before touching disk; it refuses to overwrite a directory, and without create_dirs it raises a descriptive ToolError for a missing parent rather than silently creating it.
blocks.title: read_file and write_file

blocks.anchor: def delete(root: Path, path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
blocks.text: Resolves the path, refuses to delete root itself (the extra guard beyond _resolve's containment check), and refuses a non-existent path so callers can distinguish 'already gone' from 'just deleted'. Uses shutil.rmtree for directories and Path.unlink for files.
blocks.title: delete

blocks.text: Validates timeout, clamps it to MAX_EXECUTE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, and starts the subprocess with shell=True and cwd=root. Two daemon threads (one per stream) read line by line: each accumulates into a list, enforces MAX_EXECUTE_OUTPUT_CHARS, and calls on_chunk when provided. proc.wait() with timeout is used for the main wait; on timeout, proc.kill() is called, threads are joined, and ToolError is raised.
blocks.title: execute_command: subprocess management and streaming

blocks.anchor: # tool name -> (root, params) -> result dict. daemon/connection.py's
blocks.text: READ_ONLY_TOOLS and MUTATING_TOOLS are lambda-based dicts that call each function with the right params. ALL_TOOLS merges them. _require_param raises ToolError for a missing required parameter. dispatch() looks up the tool in ALL_TOOLS and calls it, raising ToolError for both unknown tool names and any ToolError from inside the tool.
blocks.title: Tool tables and dispatch

gotchas: execute_command uses shell=True deliberately — the command is an arbitrary shell string that the person has already confirmed on the backend; it is not unsanitised input
execute_command does NOT sandbox the subprocess: cd .. or absolute paths inside the command can touch things outside root
delete refuses to delete root itself even though _resolve() would pass it (root is trivially within itself)
read_file and write_file each have a 1 MB size cap; output from execute_command is capped at 200 000 chars per stream
execute_command kills the process on timeout but still raises ToolError, so the connection gets a clean tool_result error rather than a hanging call
how_it_works: _resolve() wraps assert_within_root, translating PathGuardError into ToolError so dispatch() catches one exception type
list_dir and read_file are read-only; write_file, delete, and execute_command are mutating — both sets live in one module because they share _resolve() and the ToolError contract
execute_command runs the shell string with shell=True, cwd=root, and two reader threads (one per stream) that accumulate output line-by-line; on_chunk is called per line for Part 7 streaming
dispatch() looks the tool name up in ALL_TOOLS (the union of READ_ONLY_TOOLS and MUTATING_TOOLS) and calls it; an unknown tool name raises ToolError
inputs: root: Path (the daemon's configured allowed folder)
outputs: dict with tool-specific fields (path, entries, content, bytes_written, exit_code, etc.)
purpose: Gives daemon/connection.py's message loop the five concrete file-system and shell operations it can run on behalf of a paired MiniMe session. Every path is routed through path_guard.assert_within_root before disk access. The module is intentionally dumb and stateless: by the time a tool_call arrives here the backend has already issued a confirm, so this module just runs it.
side_effects: list_dir reads directory entries from disk
read_file reads a file from disk
write_file writes a file to disk (may create parent directories)
delete removes a file or directory tree from disk
summary: Five tool implementations (list_dir, read_file, write_file, delete, execute_command) and a dispatch table for the MiniMe local daemon.

symbols.details: Uses shell=True intentionally — the command is an already-confirmed shell string. Two daemon threads drain stdout and stderr independently to avoid one blocking the other. Each stream is capped at MAX_EXECUTE_OUTPUT_CHARS; on_chunk exceptions are silently swallowed so a broken websocket never kills the running command. On timeout the process is killed and ToolError is raised.

params.desc: maximum seconds to wait; defaults to 30, capped at 300

params.desc: optional (stream, text) callback called once per output line for live streaming; None for batch mode
params.name: on_chunk

raises: ToolError for empty command, invalid timeout, or timeout expiry

side_effects: spawns a shell subprocess with cwd=root
symbols.summary: Runs an arbitrary shell command string with cwd=root; captures stdout and stderr line by line with optional per-line streaming via on_chunk; enforces a timeout and output size cap.
